title: Unbeaten and Unbowed. India Women Win the Nations Cup and Earn Their Way Back to the Pro League.
excerpt: Five wins from five. A 2-0 final victory over hosts New Zealand in Auckland. And the prize that matters most: promotion back to the FIH Pro League after last season's relegation.
body:
The scoreline read India 2, New Zealand 0. But the significance of what happened at North Harbour Hockey Stadium in Auckland on June 21 stretches far beyond a single result.

India's women's hockey team completed a flawless campaign at the FIH Nations Cup 2025-26, winning all five matches without a loss, culminating in a composed dismantling of hosts New Zealand in the final. The victory secures their return to the FIH Pro League — the world's top-tier hockey competition — after a painful relegation at the end of last season.

## Early Dominance in the Final

India set the tone within four minutes. Navneet Kaur converted the team's first penalty corner with a powerful strike past goalkeeper Grace O'Hanlon. The early goal rattled New Zealand, and India pressed their advantage relentlessly.

In the 15th minute, Sunelita Toppo doubled the lead with a clever deflection off a fierce drag flick by Deepika. At 2-0 inside the first quarter, India were in total control — and they never let the Black Sticks back in.

New Zealand dominated possession in the second half and threw everything at the Indian defence. But the backline, anchored by the experienced Savita in goal, held firm. When New Zealand finally won a penalty corner in the fourth quarter, Savita produced a crucial save to deny Kaitlin Cotter. Even after Nikki Pradhan received a yellow card with seven minutes remaining, India's defensive structure never wavered.



> **"When New Zealand finally won a penalty corner in the fourth quarter, Savita produced a crucial save to deny Kaitlin Cotter."**


## The Road to Auckland

India's path through the tournament was comprehensive. In the group stage, they beat the USA 3-2, Japan 2-1, and Uruguay 3-2 to top Pool A — overcoming first-half deficits in two of those three matches, a sign of the team's mental resilience under pressure.

The semifinal against Chile was a statement. India scored six unanswered goals — Navneet Kaur (6', 13') and Deepika (14', 18') each struck twice in a devastating opening burst, with Neha (32') and Rutuja Pisal (36') adding the finishing touches. Captain Salima Tete was named Player of the Match for her commanding all-round display.

Deepika finished the tournament as the joint-top scorer with six goals, sharing the honour with the USA's Ashley Sessa. Lalremsiami was named Player of the Match in the final for her work-rate and link-up play.

## What Promotion Means

The Pro League return is more than a scheduling upgrade. India were relegated at the end of the 2024-25 season — a humbling moment for a programme that had made the Olympic semifinal in Tokyo and reached the quarterfinals in Paris. The Nations Cup was their route back, and they seized it emphatically.

Playing in the Pro League means regular matches against the world's top eight teams — Belgium, Netherlands, Argentina, Australia, England, Germany, and Spain. For a team trying to build consistency and close the gap with the traditional powers, that exposure is irreplaceable.

It also matters for the Hockey World Cup later this year and the long road to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket will make its debut but hockey remains one of India's strongest medal prospects.

## The Bigger Picture for Indian Women's Sport

This is India's second Nations Cup title — the first came in 2022 — and it arrives during a period of growing investment in Indian women's sport. The Hockey India League launched its women's competition, the national team has a dedicated support staff and training centre, and viewership numbers have climbed steadily since the Tokyo Olympics heroics.

For the diaspora community, the team's resurgence is a point of genuine pride. Indian women's hockey doesn't command the same headlines as cricket, but the discipline, grit, and team-first mentality this squad displays resonates with every NRI who has followed the sport's quiet rise.

*India will compete in the FIH Pro League 2026-27 season. The FIH Hockey Women's World Cup takes place later this year in the Netherlands and Belgium.*
